_about: Locked gate thresholds (CORE-1169 part 1). The lexical gate is deterministic and independent of any model/judge. Tuned on the baseline run; do not loosen without recording why.

gate._legacy_note: The absolute counts below were locked for the 20-item recorded baseline (part 1). They are infeasible on a 960-cell live run (any real run has a few boundary items), so part 2b adds RATE thresholds (gate_rates) used by evaluate_gate when n is large. The legacy counts are kept for the small recorded suites.

gate_rates._note_part2b_fix3: CORE-1169 part 2b fix #3: rate thresholds set FROM the calibration, not to make any run pass. The combined gate (after fixes #1 + #2) has a 5% false-positive rate on Nick's 20 labels (1 harder FP, 1 jargon FP). So a genuinely-plain prompt will show flags at ~5% from the gate's own residual noise; a run PASSES when its flag rates are AT OR BELOW that calibrated FP rate. median_delta_max is unchanged (the one part-1 bar the goal kept). Applied by evaluate_gate when item count exceeds min_items_for_rate.

judge._note: secondary / flag-only: never auto-fails the headline unless the lexical gate also fails

jargon._note: the BINARY jargon gate uses the sharp rarity/AoA cutoff (precision-critical); Dale-Chall is a graded signal in the difficulty score, not a binary trigger, to avoid over-flagging ordinary off-list words. jargon.py reads these values (single source of truth).
jargon._audit_core_1169_part1b: hard_zipf lowered 3.0 -> 2.6 after a live run over-flagged mid-frequency words a fluent adult knows (murmur 2.92, predictability 2.85, passivity 2.60, argumentation 2.65, ephemeral 2.99). At 2.6 the canonical academic-register failures still flag (solemnity 2.54, litotes 1.23, deontological 1.88, apperception 1.77, professionalization 2.03, iconographic 2.16). The ~2.3-2.9 band is register-dependent (rarity alone cannot separate 'solemnity' jargon from 'passivity' plain) -- the human calibration step (calibrate.py + the worksheet) measures kappa there before this referees any prompt.
jargon._aoa_note_part1c: AoA ACTIVATED (CORE-1169 part 1c): vendor/aoa_kuperman.csv fetched via download_lexicons.py (Kuperman 2012, 30,121 words; license-bound so gitignored, not committed). hard_aoa raised 10.0 -> 14.0: a word acquired after ~age 14 reads as genuinely academic register that rarity (Zipf) misses. On Nick's 20 labels this lifts the jargon-axis kappa 0.375 -> 0.519 with ZERO new false positives (cut 10 added 4 FPs; 14 is the clean optimum); it catches late-learned words like 'posit' (14.8). Tuned on n=20 so treat as provisional. AoA is kept OUT of the difficulty/delta blend (see difficulty._USE_AOA_IN_BLEND) -- in the blend it inflated archaic-source difficulty and lowered the harder-axis kappa. The register words AoA still misses (dispassionate 13.4, reframe 10.3) are the judge's job.
